senses.definition: Built for one customer or one case rather than taken off the shelf. In a platform conversation the word carries the cost with it: bespoke things never amortise.
senses.caution: The same word flatters a client and condemns a design, so know which room you are in. In front of a buyer it means premium and tailored; in an architecture review it means unrepeatable, unsupported and expensive to keep breathing. Say it about a colleague's system and you have criticised it.
senses.example: Every one of those dashboards is bespoke, which is exactly why nobody can maintain them.

cues.text: You are explaining to a sponsor why cost per client is not coming down: nothing built so far can be reused for the next one.
A client asks whether they get something built for them specifically or the same thing everyone else gets, and you want the flattering word for the first.
In an architecture review you want to name the pattern where six teams have each built their own one-off version of the same thing.
A friend had a suit made to his measurements rather than bought off the rack, and you are describing the difference to someone.
You are pricing a kitchen and the quote is enormous because every unit is made to fit that one room.

distractors: Produced in volume to a single standard, so that every unit is interchangeable with every other.
Assembled out of standard parts in a new arrangement, which is a claim about the configuration rather than about the parts themselves.
Designed so the customer can extend it themselves after delivery, through settings and plug-in points the vendor deliberately left open. The work is done by whoever bought it.
Priced individually for each buyer according to what that buyer will bear, so two customers on identical contract terms can end up paying very different amounts and neither of them knows it.

Shipped before any formal specification exists, on the argument that requirements only become clear once somebody has something in front of them. It buys speed at the price of an argument later about what was actually agreed.
